 Keys to the Game: Celtics 123, 76ers 101
 Taylor Snow ● @taylorcsnow Team Coverage Manager November 10, 2026 11:32 PM EST Key Moment
 The 76ers spent three quarters hanging at Boston’s heels Tuesday night. Then the Celtics kicked free.
 After carrying a 91-82 lead into the final frame, Boston opened the fourth quarter on a 14-0 run that put the finishing touches on a dominant 123-101 road win over its longtime rival.
 The entire run came courtesy of two players. Payton Pritchard sparked the surge with back-to-back 3-pointers before Paul George took over, pouring in eight straight points to push Boston’s advantage to 23.
 Philadelphia didn't make a field goal until the 7:37 mark of the frame, when Jaylen Brown knocked down his only 3-pointer of the night. But the damage had already been done.
 Boston continued to pour it on, extending its lead to as many as 29 points even after pulling its starters and emptying its bench.
 What had been a competitive battle through three quarters turned into a fourth-quarter blowout, as the Celtics delivered a statement victory in one of the most anticipated matchups of the young season.
 Key Player
 Paul George’s return to Philadelphia had taken a backseat to other storylines heading into Tuesday night’s showdown. By the final buzzer, however, he had stolen the spotlight.
 The nine-time All-Star erupted for a game-high 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting, including a 6-of-11 clip from 3-point range, to lead Boston past his former team. He also grabbed five rebounds and posted a plus-17 rating in 30 minutes, the best mark among Celtics starters.
 George was particularly lethal in the second and fourth quarters, scoring 13 and 14 points, respectively, during those frames.
 He saved some of his best work for last, shooting 5-of-7 from the field and 3-of-4 from deep in the final period while posting a plus-15 rating. Meanwhile, the 76ers shot just 7-of-21 as a team during the quarter.
 George’s eight consecutive points during Boston’s game-breaking run provided the knockout punch, helping to turn what had been a nine-point contest into a 23-point cushion.
 His return to Philadelphia may not have dominated the pregame conversation, but his performance made it the headline of the night.
 Box Score Nuggets
 Paul George scored a game-high 36 points, his second-highest total of the season.
 Tyrese Maxey was Philadelphia’s lone 20-point scorer, finishing with 24.
 Jayson Tatum recorded 21 points, six rebounds, four assists, and two blocks.
 Jaylen Brown tallied 13 points, five rebounds, two assists, and two steals in his first game against his former team.
 Brown finished with a game-low minus-27 rating in just under 26 minutes.
 Boston made 15 more field goals than Philadelphia, finishing with 48 makes compared to the 76ers’ 33.
 The 76ers attempted 28 free throws compared to just five by the Celtics.
 Boston outscored Philadelphia 118-77 on non-free-throw points.
 The Celtics held a 46-32 scoring advantage in the paint.
 Boston doubled Philadelphia’s 3-point output, connecting on 22 triples compared to the Sixers’ 11.
 The Celtics scored at least 29 points in all four quarters, while the 76ers reached that mark only once (31 in the third).
 Key Quote
 “He’s probably been dealing with the spotlight since he was like 12 years old … He doesn’t get enough credit for his emotional stability.”
 — Joe Mazzulla on Jayson Tatum’s handling of the most anticipated game of the season.
